reviewers.persona: Prüferin (lizenzierte Goethe-A1-Prüferin, Start Deutsch 1): Prüfungstreue, Rubrik, Aufgabenklarheit
Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: We read every German string: the Folge, the three inputs (LS1 dialogue and menu, LS2 dialogue, LS3 dialogue and e-mail), the 6 H1 texts, 2 check lines, rule cards rc.moegen and rc.akkusativ, the strategy card, instructions, situations, the S1 form and checklist, the Sp2/Sp3 cards, opening line, hint words and model turns, the redemittel, endLines, story beat and cliffhanger. We solved every item blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: gist item, 3 × 5 inputItems, 3 × 4 structuredInput, 33 pool items, 15 reserve, 6 H1, 8 check and 2 proof items (92 authored items), plus 4 perception items and the 5 S1 fields. We permuted every sentence_building item's tiles by hand against its promptDe (Aussagesatz, Frage, W-Frage). We checked every error_correction for other correct corrections. We ran the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (checkItem), on each defensible alternative: other corrections, number words, 12-hour and 24-hour times, „um …“, „Personen“ for „Leute“, and the surname alone. We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: h1 has 6 items, abc, 2 plays, text band 32–53 words, and the text variant „ein Wort, eine Zahl oder eine Uhrzeit“. sp2 is cards-ask with 2 topics. sp3 is cards-request with 2 cards, and an information question is sent back. s1 has 5 fields and a 36–48-word situation. The rubric is registries/rubrics/writing/sd1-s1.json. We recounted all H1 texts (35–48 words), the S1 situation (42) and the e-mail (55). We recomputed all arithmetic against the LS1 menu: LS2 total 2,90 + 2,60 + 3,40 + 3,80 + 4,50 + 3,70 = 20,90 ✓; t2 3,80 + 2,60 = 6,40, plus 2,50 = 8,90 ✓; t6 7,20 + 3,90 = 11,10 ✓; check 2,90 + 2,60 + 3,70 = 9,20 ✓; S1 head count Olena + 5 = 6 ✓. We checked the grammar ceiling against grammar-spine.json (g.moegen new here; möchte + infinitive licensed by g.koennen at u08 through det.moechte-infinitiv; g.possessiv-sein-ihr a1.2-u03; g.genitiv b1.1-u11). We checked the new-word load against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32; 34 lemmas here, 6 of them compounds, 17 productive) and every learner surface against the lexicons of all levels. We checked can-dos against registries/cando/a1.json, the cast against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (ensemble voices 1–2 female, 3–4 male), and the story against u08 (cliffhanger: after one hour of running, Elif offers coffee), u10 (Sophie's call, the Dresden trip the day after the birthday) and u11 (Olena: „Wir haben im Restaurant Kochi gegessen“). We compared the plan against curriculum/a1-1.md §6 u09 and a1-1.json u09, and the exemplar trail against a1.1-u04 r1–r5 and the u01, u02 and u07 round-1 reviews.

verdict: Not exit-ready: 3 BLOCKER (1 in the unit's items, 1 shared by the unit and the lexicon, 1 owned by the rule-cards file), 1 MAJOR and 11 MINOR. The unit is well built. The café scene flows on from u08's cliffhanger: an hour of running, a full café, the last fruit salad, Olena's Saturday apple cake, Elif paying, and a birthday dinner at a restaurant named after Priya's home town. It agrees with the cast bible (du among the friends, Sie with the waiter, Olena's Ukrainian surname, Sophie and Olena's WG) and with u10/u11. Every price in the unit adds up against the menu. The mag/möchte contrast of the plan is taught with real structured input (ls3-s01/s02), and the Vokalwechsel review uses nehmen, as the plan's changelog asks. The H1 block is exact to sd1.json: 6 items, 3 options, 2 plays, texts of 35–48 words, a/b/c at 2/2/2 and every distractor heard. Its tasks are original, and the „Nein, Moment …“ trap is well chosen. The Sp2, Sp3 and S1 parts match their templates. What stops exit is the correction-item class that the exemplar closed in u04 r5-F01, now in its third unit. Four of those items reject correct corrections; one is a scored Check item, and one rejects the verb its own explanation recommends. The S1 key also rejects „7.30 Uhr“ and „6 Personen“, and the rails that landed during this review turn the run red.

Each German prompt says only „Korrigieren Sie:“ and does not say what to correct. We ran checkItem.js on the alternatives, and it rejects correct corrections. Renaming the prompt cannot fix this one, because „das Verb“ admits both möchte and nehme. In ls1-p10 „Ich mag Fisch nicht.“ is WRONG. ls1-r05 and ls2-r05 are bare as well, though a second correction is unlikely there. At the start of the review the validator passed all six. The ITM-01 bare-prompt rail landed during the review and now reports all six as blockers.

findings.problem: We ran checkItem.js on the fields. f4: „7.30 Uhr“, „7:30“ and „7.30“ are WRONG, and so are „um 19.30 Uhr“, „um halb acht“ and „halb acht abends“, while „halb acht“ is right. The text gives only „halb acht“, and „7.30 Uhr“ is its exact transcription in digits. A Goethe examiner scores this field for the passende Angabe, which is the profile's own criterion. The key punishes the learner who follows the checklist („mit Zahlen“) but does not also convert to 24 hours, and it rewards the learner who ignores the checklist and writes words. f5: „6 Personen“, „sechs Personen“ and „für 6 Leute“ are WRONG, because checkNumber lets words around the digits be left out but never changed or added. „Personen“ is the word every German reservation form uses. f1: the checklist asks for the full name, but the surname alone is accepted. That is harmless, but the checklist and the key disagree. This continues the u07 r1-F03 class (a correct time form rejected by an exact:number key), now in a scored Aufgabe that claims the exam's scoring.
findings.fix: f4: accept „7.30 Uhr“, „7:30 Uhr“, „7.30“, „7:30“, „7.30 Uhr abends“, „um 19.30 Uhr“, „um 19:30 Uhr“, „um halb acht“ and „halb acht abends“. Change the checklist to „Uhrzeit: Wann essen sie?“, and give the 24-hour convention as a tip in the model text („19.30 Uhr = halb acht am Abend“), not as the key. f5: accept „6 Personen“, „sechs Personen“, „für 6 Leute“ and „für sechs Leute“. f1: change the checklist to „Name: Vorname und Familienname“, or stop accepting the surname alone.
findings.proposedRule: Extend ITM-10 over all registered courses. (1) An exact:"number" time key whose source text gives the time in words („halb acht“, „Viertel nach sieben“) accepts both the 12-hour and the 24-hour digit forms. (2) A form field accepts its own leading preposition („um“, „für“, „am“) before the digits. Failing fixture: a1.1-u09 ls6 f4 „7.30 Uhr“. A note for the rubric owner: the zero rule form-number-exact compares `given` with one `expected` string once spaces are removed. It must compare against every accepted form, or „19:30“ and „halb acht“ will also score 0 once the S1 scorer is wired.

findings.problem: This is the u04 r1-F26/r2-F03 and u02 r1-F11 class: string matching solves the items, so they do not force processing of the form. In ls1-s04 the key is the name in the stem. Its explanation names no rule that excludes „Priya“, since „du magst“ is also one person; only „Priya und Olena“ is excluded by the form. In ls3-s03 the only option with möchte answers a question with möchten. In ls1-s03 the key is the only option in OVS order, so it is the odd one out by shape. With two case-ambiguous nouns, „Obst findet Elif gut“ can also be read literally as „the fruit likes Elif“. The explanation's „…, immer“ is not idiomatic.
findings.fix: ls1-s04: make the ending decide, e.g. „Sie hören: ‚… mag Fisch sehr.‘ Wer kann das sein?“ with the options „Olena“ / „Olena und Elif“ / „ihr“. ls3-s03: keep the stem and give the options „Ich mag Fisch mit Kartoffeln.“ / „Fisch mit Kartoffeln, bitte.“ / „Ja, Fisch mag ich.“, with the key „Fisch mit Kartoffeln, bitte.“ ls1-s03: key „Elif findet Obst gut.“, explanation „‚Ich mag Obst.‘ heißt: Elif findet Obst immer gut. (c) The fruit salad is called „nicht teuer“ at the highest breakfast price on the menu. (d) LS2 asks again for the order that LS1 has settled. It then goes straight from ordering to „Wir möchten bezahlen“, before anyone has eaten. findings.quote: „Und die Leute dort sind sehr höflich.“ (dialogue and invitation e-mail) · „Am Freitag habe ich am Abend Zeit.“ · „Dann essen wir auch etwas. Laufen macht müde!“ · e-mail „Ich brauche die Antwort bis Mittwoch.“ · openingLine „Zuerst Teil 2: Fragen und Antworten, erst zum Thema …, dann zum Thema …. Dann Teil 3 im Café.“ · „Möchten Sie vielleicht einen Apfelkuchen?“ / „Bestellen Sie ein Getränk und einen Kuchen.“
findings.problem: Nothing here is wrong German, but several lines on model surfaces are off-idiom. Nobody recommends a restaurant, or invites friends to one, because the staff are „höflich“. The word is forced in for lx.hoeflich; „nett“ or „freundlich“ is what people say. „Am Freitag habe ich am Abend Zeit“ doubles the time phrase. „Laufen macht müde“ is given as the reason to eat, when hunger is the reason. „die Antwort“ from several friends sounds odd; „eure Antwort“ is above the ceiling. The opening line stacks zuerst, erst, dann and Dann. At the café the order is „ein Stück (Apfel)kuchen“. „einen Kuchen“ is heard, but the unit never shows the standard form, although lx.stueck is known from u04 and „Kaffee und Kuchen“ is the plan's Landeskunde point.
findings.fix: „Und die Leute dort sind sehr nett.“ (dialogue and e-mail); keep höflich where it is true, e.g. in the rm06 function „jemanden höflich ansprechen“. „Am Freitagabend habe ich Zeit.“ „Laufen macht hungrig!“ or „Ich habe Hunger!“. E-mail: „Wer kommt mit? Ich brauche bis Mittwoch eine Antwort von allen.“ (the ihr-imperative „Antwortet bis Mittwoch!“ is licensed only from a1.2-u09). Opening line: „Hallo! Zuerst Teil 2: zwei Themen, ‚Essen und Trinken‘ und ‚Getränke‘. Dann Teil 3 im Café. Sie fangen an!“ Waiter: „Möchten Sie vielleicht ein Stück Apfelkuchen?“, with the explanation keeping „einen Apfelkuchen“ as the short spoken form.

findings.quote: Sp3 „Sie und Ihre Partnerin sind im Café. … Mit Ihren Karten bestellen Sie etwas und bitten um die Rechnung.“ · learner „Wir möchten bezahlen. Die Rechnung, bitte.“ – partner „Gern. Hier ist die Rechnung.“ · partner „Die Speisekarte, bitte.“ / „Kann ich bitte den Zucker haben?“ · Sp2 „Sagen Sie auch: Was mögen Sie? Was mögen Sie nicht?“ · learner model only „Ja, Fisch mag ich sehr.“ / „Ja, ich mag Kaffee.“
findings.problem: In sd1.sp3 two candidates each make a request for an object and react to one. The café frame here makes the partner switch roles within one round. The partner serves the coffee and hands over the bill, which a waiter does, and then asks for the menu and the sugar, which a guest does. „Wir möchten bezahlen“ is spoken to the person who is supposedly paying with the learner. The u04 exemplar keeps Sp3 neutral („Ich möchte ein Brot, bitte.“ / „Ja, hier, bitte.“). The hint words leave out „Kann ich bitte … haben?“, the request form the plan names for this Sp3. In Sp2 the situation and the can-do (cd.a1.essen-vorlieben: „… und was ich nicht mag“) ask for a dislike, but no model turn shows one. The partner's persona dislikes fish, but nobody asks her about it.
findings.fix: Sp3: drop „im Café“ and „bestellen“ from the situation („Sie und Nora haben je zwei Karten. Bitten Sie Nora um die Sache auf Ihrer Karte.“). Make the learner's bill turn „Kann ich bitte die Rechnung haben?“ – „Ja, hier, bitte.“, and add „Kann ich bitte … haben?“ to hintWords. Sp2: make one learner answer a dislike, e.g. partner „Mögen Sie Fisch?“ – learner „Nein, Fisch mag ich nicht. Aber ich esse gern Käse.“

findings.quote: h1-06 „Was bezahlt der Mann?“ options „den Salat und das Bier“ / „den Kuchen und den Tee“ / „alles zusammen“ · keys c, b, a, c, b, a
findings.problem: sd1.json's text variant for the scaffolded H1 allows three short answers, each a word, a number or a time, standing in for pictures. h1-06 offers two-noun accusative phrases and „alles zusammen“, which no picture can show. The item is fine as a listening task, but it trains a Teil 1 shape the exam never shows. The six keys run c-b-a-c-b-a. The balance is 2/2/2 and ITM-03 passes, but a strict period is a positional pattern of the u04 r2-F04 kind.
findings.fix: h1-06: „Was isst der Mann?“ with the options „Salat“ / „Kuchen“ / „Suppe“, keeping t6. Or keep the question and give picture-able options („Salat und Bier“ / „Kuchen und Tee“ / „Salat und Tee“). Break the period, e.g. by swapping h1-04's options so that its key is a.

findings.quote: focus „Wortakzent in Komposita: Das erste Wort hat den Akzent – APFELkuchen, OBSTsalat, TOMATENsuppe.“ · x01–x04 „Hören Sie: ‚…‘. Welches Wort hat den Akzent?“ keys Apfel, Tomaten, Obst, Käse
findings.problem: All four perception items have the same answer, the first part, and the focus line states that rule on the same screen. They can be solved without listening, and after the first item they no longer train perception.
findings.fix: Pair the simple word with its compound, so that the stress moves and must be heard. Examples: „Salat“ (sa-LAT) against „Obstsalat“ (OBST-), and „Tomate“ (to-MA-te) against „Tomatensuppe“. Ask „Wo ist der Akzent: am Anfang oder am Ende?“, or ask which of two recordings stresses correctly.

findings.problem: These are the word cards the learner studies in this unit, and each nudges against the story. The birthday of the unit is Olena's, on Friday. The card gives Arjun a birthday on Saturday, the day of the Dresden trip in u10, where nobody mentions it; casts/series.json puts Arjun's party at the end of A1.2. The unit's café serves breakfast until twelve, and the card says eleven. In the unit Priya never asks for the menu, because the waiter brings it. None of these is a contradiction on its own, since the cards are generic sentences. But the u01 r1-F07 and u02 r1-F04 reviews show how quickly such cards are read as story facts.
